newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Ramos will step down in 1998 even if the Supreme Court decides to allow the People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action (Pirma) to campaign for a plebiscite on lifting term limits of elective officials. (INQUIRER)

- Singaporean Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong arrived last night for a three-day state visit, signifying the full restoration of Philippine-Singapore relations which were badly strained by widespread anger here over the 1995 execution of Flor Contemplacion. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Agents of the National Bureau of Investigation yesterday said they have documents in their possession which could help solve the murder of journalist Danny Hernandez. (JOURNAL)

- The Philippine Central Bank is set to formally inform the International Monetary Fund the country can comply with its exit programme only by October this year when Congress would have completed the comprehensive tax reform programme. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- American Overseas Private Investment Corp has upgraded the Philippines' rating by removing it from a list of countries that require a host of government guarantees before it will extend its own protection. (MALAYA/STANDARD/TIMES)
- The yields on Treasury bills took a further across-the-board plunge yesterday in the aftermath of good economic indicators. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
